item.title: Why the Pentagon Is Eyeing a Hydrogen-Powered Drone
item.description: A fuel cell-powered drone can operate longer than a battery-powered one, and more quietly than a gas-powered one—giving it a decisive edge in aerial operations. The post Why the Pentagon Is Eyeing a Hydrogen-Powered Drone appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The F-35 Fighter Jet Can’t Maneuver Too Well. That’s Not Really a Problem.
item.description: The F-35 was not built to win dogfights, but to operate smoothly at long ranges and over long periods of time. The post The F-35 Fighter Jet Can’t Maneuver Too Well. That’s Not Really a Problem. appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Royal Navy’s First Autonomous Helicopter Just Took Flight
item.description: Though autonomous helicopters like the Proteus are still cutting-edge technology, they are expected to play a major role in the Royal Navy’s operations in the near future. The post The Royal Navy’s First Autonomous Helicopter Just Took Flight appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: US Navy Veteran Sentenced to Five Years in Russian Prison for Arms Smuggling
item.description: Charles Zimmerman recently docked his yacht at Sochi, Russia—and inadvertently brought a rifle with him, resulting in his imprisonment. The post US Navy Veteran Sentenced to Five Years in Russian Prison for Arms Smuggling appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: US Navy F/A-18 vs. US Air Force F-16: Which Fighter Jet Rules the Sky?
item.description: In essence, the F-16 is faster and more maneuverable, while the F/A-18 is built for survival. But which one would actually win in a fight? The post US Navy F/A-18 vs. US Air Force F-16: Which Fighter Jet Rules the Sky? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How the Airbus A330 MRTT Could Change Aerial Refueling Forever
item.description: The MRTT program has several key advantages over comparable aircraft like the KC-135—chiefly its ability to draw from civilian supply chains for upkeep. The post How the Airbus A330 MRTT Could Change Aerial Refueling Forever appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: “SERE”: How American Pilots Prepare for Being Shot Down
item.description: In past wars, captured American pilots were subjected to extreme hardship and used for propaganda purposes. Today, the US Air Force is preparing its fighter pilots for similar conditions. The post “SERE”: How American Pilots Prepare for Being Shot Down appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Could the Navy’s FF(X) Frigate See Service by 2028?
item.description: The FF(X) program could fill in for the ill-fated Constellation class, which saw cancellation last year after producing only two of the frigates. The post Could the Navy’s FF(X) Frigate See Service by 2028? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How “Drone Kill Zones” Could Save Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine’s sophisticated anti-personnel drone network has effectively frozen the Russian advance near Kupiansk—a promising sign that its tactics could be copied elsewhere. The post How “Drone Kill Zones” Could Save Ukraine appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why the US Needs to Rethink Its Hopes for Saudi Arabia
item.description: Despite many US inducements, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has turned away from normalization with Israel and broader US alignment in the Middle East. The post Why the US Needs to Rethink Its Hopes for Saudi Arabia appeared first on The National Interest.
